check_red_at_base: quality-harness's declared check (bash scripts/selftest.sh) fails at this commit in the tree bench builds (measured 2026-10-14): lifecycle.test.mjs 'reported: a scratch corpus does not pull the record gates' fails even in a full-history clone, and two orphan-sweep.test.mjs cases that read git history fail in the single-commit tree
instruction: CI moves to Python 3.13 on Linux and macOS; the Windows job stays on Python 3.12 for now. In .github/workflows/selftest.yml, the selftest, coverage and mutations jobs set up python-version '3.13'; the windows job keeps '3.12'. Then update the two documents that state the CI version. In README.md, the Requirements line about Python becomes exactly: - Python 3.9 or newer; CI tests 3.13, and 3.12 on Windows. In docs/INSTALL.md, in the Python row of the table, the last cell (What is actually tested) becomes exactly: **3.13** on Linux and macOS, **3.12** on Windows — the only versions CI runs. Change nothing else.

require.match: (?m)^- Python 3\.9 or newer; CI tests 3\.13, and 3\.12 on Windows\.$
(?m)^\| Python \| 3\.9 or newer, by syntax: .* \| \*\*3\.13\*\* on Linux and macOS, \*\*3\.12\*\* on Windows — the only versions CI runs\. \|$
